overlays.scope: Explicit broader existing Lagu Timur overlap; musical/source/photo/control fields unchanged

exact_changes.old: Lagu Manado is a regional song-repertoire field. Firsthand concert witness Yudi Latif expressly identifies O Ina Ni Keke as a traditional song from Manado; composer identifies North Sulawesi material. Existing Indonesian folk and Indonesian pop are broad national fields, not limited to their selected acoustic-duo/retro-band examples. Queued Indonesian Indigenous Traditional remains a broad national heritage category, and Lagu Aceh a different positively identified regional repertoire. None is asserted mutually exclusive; the positive regional repertoire axis supplies distinction rather than piano instrumentation, composer nationality or different artist alone. No exact EveryNoise artist membership or exclusive city origin is asserted.
exact_changes.new: Lagu Manado is a regional song-repertoire field. Existing Indonesian folk and Indonesian pop are broad national fields, not limited to their selected acoustic-duo/retro-band examples. Queued Indonesian Indigenous Traditional remains a broad national heritage category, and Lagu Aceh a different positively identified regional repertoire. None is asserted mutually exclusive; the positive regional repertoire axis supplies distinction rather than piano instrumentation, composer nationality or different artist alone. No exact EveryNoise artist membership or exclusive city origin is asserted. Actual existing lagu_timur is a broader cross-regional Eastern Indonesian contemporary-song field and explicitly acknowledges narrower Manado/Maluku overlap. The proposed Manado regional repertoire is not presented as missing from that umbrella; its positive named repertoire axis is narrower, not an assertion that all Lagu Timur is one artist or one island.

exact_changes.old: Complete Ananda Sukarlan Rapsodia Nusantara no.8, selected as the independently named concluding work of Agus Sandjaya’s 12 April2019 solo pianoforte programme at St Stephen’s Friday Music, Sydney. The presenter lists only Sandjaya/pianoforte for this date. Other named works and other dates’ euphonium or organ players are outside this complete-work scope. Retain one pianist, one piano and zero vocal parts. Composer’s own2013 notes identify the finished eighth rhapsody as variations on O Inani Keke from North Sulawesi; his early2011 provisional numbering concerned a different work and is not transferred. This is a concert transformation of the regional song, not a claim that all Manado songs are instrumental. Lagu Manado is a regional song-repertoire field. Broad artMusic applies only to this fixed composed concert work, not all regional song. Original folk tuning, sung language, global temperament, microphone chain and actual recording venue are not inferred. Controlled live-room listening presentation is authored.
